We have a target molecule: C=C(C1=CC=C(OC)C=C1)C2=CC=C(OC)C=C2. This is a stilbene derivative with two anisole (methoxy phenyl) groups attached to a central double bond (trans? but not specified). The retrosynthesis step found a template (ID 223474) that matches and when applied gives two precursors: 'COc1ccc(Br)cc1' and 'COc1ccc(C(C)=O)cc1'. So the reaction is a coupling of a bromo anisole with an acetophenone derivative? Actually the product is the stilbene with two anisole groups. The template appears to be a Heck-type coupling? The precursors: anisole bromide (p-bromo anisole) and anisole acetyl (p-methoxyacetophenone). The product is the alkene formed via a Heck reaction between aryl bromide and aryl ketone? The template shows Br-aryl + O=C-CH3-aryl -> alkene with central double bond and loss of CO? Wait the product is C=C(Ar)Ar. The template: Br-aryl + O=C-CH3-aryl -> CH2= C(Ar)Ar (with loss of CO and CH3?). Actually the retro template: [CH2]=[C](-aryl)-aryl << Br-aryl . O=C-CH3-aryl . So the forward reaction is a coupling of aryl bromide with aryl methyl ketone to give stilbene and CO? This is a known reaction: McMurry? Not exactly. But we have precursors.

Now we need to ensure leaves are commercially available and total price <= $150. Need to check buyability and maybe price. Use is_buyable tool for the two SMILES.
